title: The reclaim policy reads protocol state to decide a connection is idle, but the request using it has moved to the upstream
index_line: T-0094 · MEM_WRITE · HTTP/2 connection reclaimed under slot pressure while its request is proxying upstream → UAF · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: Connection reclamation assumed the protocol state is the whole truth about liveness: a connection with no active streams is idle and may be freed. But a request that has opened an upstream connection is exactly when the client-side connection must stay alive — its memory is still referenced by the upstream code path, which the reclaim policy never consults.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated HTTP/2 request is served through a proxy_pass, so nginx opens an upstream connection
under worker_connections pressure, the reclaim policy marks connections reusable from protocol state (no active streams)
nginx closes the request's own HTTP/2 connection and frees its memory while the upstream request is in flight
the upstream completion path continues to dereference the freed connection structure
attacker-shaped heap reuse places controlled data where the stale pointer is used, turning the use-after-free into control-flow hijack

source.protocol.value: HTTP/2 client connection multiplexed with a proxy_pass upstream request

lifetime.object.value: the freed HTTP/2 connection structure still referenced by upstream processing

sync.window.value: the worker's finite connection-slot budget (worker_connections) whose pressure triggers reclamation

guard.none.value: no check that the connection is unreferenced by an in-flight upstream request before freeing

preconditions.expr: HTTP/2 is enabled and requests are proxied to an upstream
the build is in the affected range (1.19.7 through 1.31.8)
the worker reuses connections under slot pressure (reachable by exhausting worker_connections)

check.spec: grep -E 'worker_connections' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf 2>/dev/null; printf 'pressure = open many concurrent TLS connections from one source\n'

success: worker crash in the upstream completion path after many short-lived HTTP/2 connections from one source
response data from another request's freed structure, or controlled control-flow on a shaped heap
failure_like: HTTP/2 disabled, or no upstream proxying configured
the build keeps the connection referenced until upstream completion
false_positive: worker crashes under load have many causes — require the pattern of many short TLS connections plus HTTP/2 proxying and the crash site in the connection-reclaim path
connection statistics climbing alone is not exploitation

hazards: any multiplexed server that reclaims resources from protocol state while a second subsystem still holds a reference
slot/limit pressure is the lever: reclamation runs exactly when the attacker can create contention
the freeing subsystem and the using subsystem each believe they own the lifetime
non_transfers: reference-counted connection objects where the upstream holds a counted reference
servers without HTTP/2 or without proxying

evidence.target: nginx HTTP/2 connection reclamation with upstream proxying, 1.19.7-1.31.8 (CVE-2026-123633, nginx2root)

provenance.author: Wiz Research
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-123633: HTTP/2 connection use-after-free — a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, affecting reverse-proxy processing when available connection slots run low; demonstrated RCE with an ASLR bypass; reported 2026-10-21

provenance.author: Xint (nginx2root)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-123633: a use-after-free caused by an active HTTP/2 connection remaining eligible for draining — when a request opens an upstream connection, nginx can close the request's own HTTP/2 connection and free its memory while upstream code keeps accessing it; requires an upstream (affects 1.19.7+)

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-123633 description (HTTP/2 UAF in the worker when proxying client requests to a backend)
